page: Microsoft Azure D64as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dasv7 server family. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, this instance features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This server does not include local storage but is Premium Storage capable, allowing for external high-performance disk attachments. No GPU hardware is present on this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64as_v7 demonstrates strong CPU and memory capabilities. Single-core performance via stress-ng and single-threaded compression/decompression tasks rank in the top 10% tier. Multi-core processing and memory bandwidth tests, including uncached read and write operations, consistently place in the top 25% tier. Database operations measured via Passmark also achieve top-tier status, while Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput register in the top 25%. For machine learning workloads, the instance achieves top-tier text generation speeds with medium-sized 7B LLM models, though performance drops to average levels when processing larger 70B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D64as_v7 offers a dense allocation of high-frequency AMD EPYC compute resources and balanced memory capacity without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. This makes it a viable option for workloads that require high CPU throughput and moderate memory density. Appropriate workloads for this configuration include relational databases, enterprise web serving, multi-threaded data compression, and medium-scale language model inference.
